Sandbox_LugliDMS_Enabled_tooltip: Some buildings hide a stash box in a back room: a nailed crate, a locked lockbox or a padlocked footlocker, each with its own ways in, that pays out a good haul once you get it open. A lockbox or footlocker has a key, left in the same building or on a zombie nearby. Off: no new box is hidden. Boxes already in this world stay and can still be opened.
Sandbox_LugliDMS_StashChance_tooltip: Out of every hundred buildings, how many hide a stash box. A remote farm or cabin hides one more often, a crowded city block less often; 100 is every building. Each building is judged once, the first time you come near it.
Sandbox_LugliDMS_MaxPerBuilding_tooltip: The most stash boxes one building can hide. A building hides one, and one more for every 1,000 tiles of floor plan, up to this number, so a home hides one and a large store a few. Each goes in a different room.
Sandbox_LugliDMS_PayoutRolls_tooltip: A stash box rolls one loot list per step of quality: once when Ordinary, twice when Good, three times when Rich. Each point here adds that many rolls again. 0 is the balanced default.
Sandbox_LugliDMS_BruteDamage_tooltip: What opening a box by force does to what is inside: glass and fragile things break, tools and weapons lose condition. Only Smash, Force and a sledgehammer can damage what is inside, and forcing a lid is gentler than smashing. Every other way in never damages anything.
Sandbox_LugliDMS_NoiseScale_tooltip: Scales how far the noise of every way in carries, while the work goes on and when it ends, and of picking a door. Zombies inside that distance hear it. 0 is silent. A safe's alarm is not scaled.
Sandbox_LugliDMS_TimeScale_tooltip: Scales how long every way of opening a box or a safe takes, and picking a door.
Sandbox_LugliDMS_SafeChance_tooltip: Out of every hundred offices, pawn shops and big houses, how many hide a dial safe. Judged apart from the stash boxes, and never more than one safe per building.
Sandbox_LugliDMS_VaultSafeChance_tooltip: Out of every hundred banks, police stations, jewelry stores, pharmacies and gun stores, how many keep a keypad safe in a back room. They are far fewer than offices, so this is much higher than the safe chance. Out in the country more often, in a crowded city less often.
Sandbox_LugliDMS_SafeTries_tooltip: How many wrong codes a safe takes before it locks you out for a while.
Sandbox_LugliDMS_SafeLockoutHours_toolti: How many in-game hours a keypad safe refuses every code after too many wrong ones. A dial safe locks for half as long. Never under one in-game minute, even at 0.
Sandbox_LugliDMS_SafeAlarm_tooltip: A keypad safe that locks you out, or that you fail to hotwire, sets off a loud alarm that draws zombies from far away.
Sandbox_LugliDMS_CluesPerSafe_tooltip: How many notes with a hint to the code each safe leaves behind, in the same building or on a zombie nearby. One note alone still leaves many codes possible, two together leave a handful (3 to 10) to try, and no set of notes ever gives the whole code. 0: no notes, so drilling, the blow torch, cracking the dial or hotwiring the keypad are the ways in.
Sandbox_LugliDMS_DebugLog_tooltip: Writes a line to the console for every container sealed and opened. For troubleshooting only.
